main_body: Large green tile hip roof (rows ~4-42) over a red-beam, cream-plaster wall with a lattice double door (rows ~43-74) on a stone base
top_band: Roof slope: green tiles in several tones, with a lighter ridge band at rows 4-8, running to the eave at row ~42; about 34 rows of foreshortened top surface
evidence: Reading down the middle column: the golden ridge caps and light-green ridge band, then the large tiled roof slope (rows 8-42) that clearly reads as a horizontal-ish top surface. A dark eave row at ~40-42 sits above the bright orange beam top at row 43, which acts as the front-edge line. Below it is the vertical wall face with posts, a dark inset lattice door and cream panels, then the stone base. The roof is a big visible top surface and the wall is a distinct front face, so this matches the building references and passes the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 green steps with per-tile highlights and the outline is tinted dark green or brown, so it is not a sticker look. However, the tile pattern is a very regular, mechanical grid, unlike the clumped, varied reference roofs. The cream wall panels are large areas (well over 5x5 px) of nearly one colour with only a few sparse speckles, and the red posts and beam and the grey base are mostly flat fills. Many wall tiles carry only about 3-4 colours, so the building is flatter and less information-rich than the references (timber framing, speckled plaster, individually shaded stones). It would look thinner next to them.
